scope: 1 UE, real CUDA gNB and original CPU srsUE, 20 MHz / 23.04 MS/s / 1x1, original channel backend and fixed historical input bundle. HTML reports were not modified.
mechanism: After input stalls or other delays, RealTimePacer carries at most one nominal batch of lateness (1 ms here). Greater lateness rebases the deadline instead of licensing an unbounded catch-up burst. Samples remain intact; unrecovered wall-clock lag persists in the achieved radio/wall ratio.
limits: CSV write syscall elapsed time includes kernel filesystem work and time off CPU; it does not alone prove a physical NVMe service-time bottleneck.
The instrumented and uninstrumented results are one run each; trace overhead is not a constant correction to subtract from other configurations.
Sparse attribution proves which producer stage dominates each rebase, not whether delayed input originated in UE compute, transport or receiver dispatch.
The historical 0.9975 report used warmup-inclusive control-tag endpoints; after warmup it was 0.9989. Early slow periods amplify the displayed whole-span deficit.
Independent rare delays can vary by run; the 16.15 ms reconciliation applies to the sparse diagnostic run, not the earlier 9.83 ms clean run.
